page_map.layout_notes: Pages 1-10 are the main paper; pages 11-13 are single-column references. The main text is predominantly two-column; Figures 1, 5, and 6 and tables form wide visual anchors. No appendix or supplementary pages occur before References.

abstract_sentences.text: Monocular normal estimation aims to estimate the normal map from a single RGB image of an object under arbitrary lights.

evidence.anchor: single RGB image of an object under arbitrary lights

abstract_sentences.text: Existing methods rely on deep models to directly predict normal maps.
However, they often suffer from 3D misalignment: while the estimated normal maps may appear to have a correct appearance, the reconstructed surfaces often fail to align with the 3D geometry.

We argue that this misalignment stems from the current paradigm: the model struggles to distinguish and estimate varying geometry represented in normal maps, as the differences in underlying geometry are reflected only through relatively subtle color variations.
To address this issue, we propose a new paradigm that reformulates normal estimation as shading sequence estimation, where shading sequences are more sensitive to various geometry information.

evidence.anchor: reformulates normal estimation as shading sequence estimation

abstract_sentences.text: By learning to infer the shading sequence of an object, the model can better capture underlying 3D geometry and thereby produce more accurate normal predictions.

Building on this paradigm, we present RoSE, a method that leverages image-to-video generative models to predict shading sequences, which are then converted into normal maps by solving a simple ordinary least-squares problem.
To enhance robustness and better handle complex objects, RoSE is trained on a synthetic dataset, MultiShade, with diverse shapes, materials, and light conditions.

evidence.anchor: diverse shapes, materials, and light conditions

abstract_sentences.text: Experiments demonstrate that RoSE achieves state-of-the-art performance on both synthetic and real-world benchmark datasets for object-based monocular normal estimation.

introduction_moves.move: context: normal maps encode surface orientation and motivate applications in relighting, 3D reconstruction, and rendering; monocular estimation avoids specialized hardware cost.
problem: direct RGB-to-normal deep models can look visually correct while being inconsistent with underlying 3D geometry; subtle color differences make fine detail hard to distinguish.

evidence.anchor: fail to remain consistent with the underlying 3D geometry

introduction_moves.move: failure_of_prior_work and missing_insight: Figure 2 shows over-smooth surfaces, while Figure 3 contrasts geometry sensitivity of shading sequence and normal representations using TV.
core_idea: propose a clamped normal-light dot-product sequence that preserves geometry cues while excluding material influence and can be converted back to normals with OLS.
method_preview: treat the sequence as a video, use an image-to-video generative model, recover normals with OLS, and train on MultiShade for complex materials and lights.

evidence.anchor: rich lighting priors encoded in large-scale video models

introduction_moves.move: result_preview: claim superior performance to state-of-the-art methods without reporting a number, uncertainty, or failure count.
contribution_list: enumerate the new paradigm, RoSE with canonical parallel lights and analytic derivation, and MultiShade plus multi-dataset SOTA results.

related_work_moves.move: taxonomy and nearest_neighbor_contrast: classify monocular-normal methods from handcrafted/conventional deep to generative, physics-inspired, autoregressive, and multi-light generation; position shading supervision as a response to 3D misalignment and generated-image artifacts.

evidence.anchor: In contrast, we propose a new paradigm

related_work_moves.move: chronology and nearest_neighbor_contrast: summarize video generation architectures and contrast NormalCrafter's per-frame normals for an input video with this paper's single-image, predefined-light-path shading sequence.

evidence.anchor: predict a shading sequence that follows a predefined light path

related_work_moves.move: credit_or_foundation and gap_creation: cite photometric-stereo work showing learned features resemble shading sequences, then make sequence supervision the training target.

evidence.anchor: learned features closely resemble shading sequences

method_moves.move: setup_notation and define_component: define shading map as clamped normal-light dot products and the multi-light shading sequence; state that reflectance and cast-shadow effects are removed while geometry cues remain.

evidence.anchor: Shading maps remove the effects of surface reflectance

method_moves.move: state_problem and contrast_alternative: express direct monocular estimation as Φ:I→N and describe bias introduced by first generating RGB images under simple lights.

evidence.anchor: generating additional RGB images itself introduces substantial bias

method_moves.move: derive: define ΦS:Ig→Ss and derive the OLS shading-to-normal solution.

evidence.anchor: The solution is unique when L is full rank

method_moves.move: explain_mechanism and connect_to_prediction: identify clamp-induced OLS bias and retain only positive shading equations.
state_complexity/guarantee: require at least three positive shadings from non-coplanar lights, choose a 45-degree upper-hemisphere ring-light, and state Lemma 1's six-light lower bound.

evidence.anchor: the minimum number of lights is lmin = m × n = 6

method_moves.move: connect_to_experiment: report non-monotone light-count observations—nine lights improve over six by 0.74 degrees on LUCES, while twelve lose 1.31 degrees.

evidence.anchor: The best performance was achieved with 9 light sources

method_moves.move: instantiate_algorithm and give_intuition: instantiate gθ as a video diffusion U-Net producing a grayscale sequence conditioned on grayscale input; Figure 5 supplies the pipeline.
define_component: combine global CLIP cross-attention with local VAE-latent concatenation, replicate grayscale to three channels, decode and average channels.

evidence.anchor: combines global guidance from CLIP embedding and local guidance from VAE latent concatenation

method_moves.move: derive and instantiate_algorithm: train in latent space with z0=E(Ss), zt=αtε+σtz0, and the one-step denoised z-hat0 diffusion loss.

evidence.anchor: standard training objectives on latent space

method_moves.move: connect_to_experiment: curate MultiShade from 90K Objaverse models with three light families, six views, view-dependent transforms, MatSynth augmentation, 576×576 Blender renders, and approximately three million pairs.

experimental_design.name: research_questions
experimental_design.description: The paper does not pre-list numbered hypotheses; its sections operationalize benchmark effectiveness, sequence quality, unseen-distribution robustness, and component/data/path attribution.

experimental_design.name: datasets_and_tasks
experimental_design.description: Object-based monocular normal estimation is evaluated on DiLiGenT, LUCES, and a 100-object unseen Objaverse test set; DiLiGenT is parallel-light and LUCES near-field.

experimental_design.name: baselines
experimental_design.description: Seven monocular-normal baselines are listed: GeoWizard, DSINE, StableNormal, Lotus-G, Lotus-D, Neural LightRig, and NiRNE.

experimental_design.name: benchmark_sampling
experimental_design.description: For each DiLiGenT/LUCES object, ten relatively centered-light images are selected; the indices are said to be in the appendix.

experimental_design.name: multishade_test_protocol
experimental_design.description: MultiShade test uses 100 unseen Objaverse objects, random MatSynth-test materials, one point, one directional, two environment lights, seven views, and 2,800 samples.

experimental_design.name: implementation_and_hardware
experimental_design.description: Training uses 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs with 80GB memory; the video architecture follows prior work.

claim_closure.claim: Shading sequences are more geometry-sensitive and can replace normal-map supervision.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations (1), (3), (4), Figure 3, and positive-shading OLS filtering.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3 TV and Table 4/5 diagnostics support sensitivity and detail alignment, but baseline sequence metrics are derived from predicted normals.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates the reformulation but does not separately resolve the independent mechanism test.

evidence.anchor: align with the results of normal estimation

claim_closure.claim: RoSE maps one image to a useful shading sequence and then a normal map.
claim_closure.method_response: Figure 5, dual CLIP/VAE conditioning, latent diffusion loss, and OLS.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–3 and Table 6 report normal/threshold performance across benchmark and synthetic settings.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion explicitly recovers RoSE, image-to-video generation, analytic solver, and SOTA claim.

evidence.anchor: Experiments show that our method outperforms state-of-the-art methods

claim_closure.claim: Canonical ring lights make the OLS reconstruction identifiable.
claim_closure.method_response: Full-rank OLS, positive-shading filtering, 45° ring setup, and Lemma 1.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Lemma 1 states six-light lower bound; 9/12-light observations and spiral ablation probe practical path choices.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not repeat the light-count result, but no contradictory result is reported for the main ring path.

evidence.anchor: The solution is unique when L is full rank
minimum number of lights is lmin = m × n = 6

claim_closure.method_response: 90K Objaverse models, three lighting families, six views, and MatSynth material augmentation.
claim_closure.evidence_response: MultiShade Table 3 and w/o MA/Lotus-G+M/Ours+L ablations support an average effect but show small and object-dependent dataset effects.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls MultiShade large-scale and diverse, without resolving split/overlap or object heterogeneity.

claim_closure.method_response: Seven baseline comparisons and common MAE protocol.

measurement_disagreements.name: reference_boundary_and_word_count
measurement_disagreements.description: The automatic measurement row for this PDF reports 13 pages, approximately 6,520 English words, 4 figure captions, 6 table captions, 5 numbered equations, and 1 theorem/lemma item, but its spaced-small-caps reference regex leaves main_end_page_provisional at 13. Manual PDF inspection places References at physical page 11, so main pages are 1–10 and reference pages 11–13; the automatic 6,520 count is retained only as a cross-check, while section estimates are manual.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Direct RGB-to-normal prediction is reframed as grayscale-to-canonical-light shading-sequence prediction; a video diffusion model generates the sequence, and positive-shading/full-rank OLS analytically recovers normals. The chain runs from 3D misalignment on pp.1–3 through Eqs. (1)–(5)/Lemma 1 on pp.4–6 to Tables 1–6 on pp.7–10. [p.1–5, Abstract/Introduction/Methods, `reformulates normal estimation as shading sequence estimation`; explicit]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the failure visualization, sensitivity diagnostic, reversible formulation, ring-light lower bound, pipeline, MultiShade scale, three evaluation settings, SNE/shading diagnostics, ablations, and explicit limitations. [pp.2–10, Figures 2–6/Tables 1–6/Discussion; explicit]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Rendering/camera/augmentation details, benchmark image indices, additional qualitative analyses, and additional experiments are called out but no appendix appears before References; this preserves the conceptual story but prevents independent reproduction. [pp.6–11, appendix calls and `REFERENCES`; layout_observation/interpretation]
final_judgment.best_pattern: The strongest pattern is visible failure → representation-level diagnostic → reversible definition/solver bridge → pipeline → task results → mechanism/detail diagnostics → component ablations. [pp.2–10, Figures 2–6 and Tables 1–6; interpretation grounded in layout]
final_judgment.largest_gap: The main unresolved gap is mechanism identification: Table 4's other-method shading maps are computed from predicted normals, while single-run tables omit uncertainty; Table 3's object/sample denominator is also unspecified. [pp.8–10, Table 3/4/6 and surrounding text; interpretation]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For an intermediate-representation claim, pair a visible diagnostic with a reversible bridge and matched task/mechanism/ablation evidence, and report heterogeneity and uncertainty with the decision metric. [pp.2–5, pp.7–10; interpretation]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies when the intermediate signal has an explicit inverse and matched controls are possible; if evaluation is derived from the final output or data/randomness cannot be matched, diagnostics establish association rather than causal attribution. [p.4 OLS conditions; pp.8–9 Table 4 construction; interpretation]

reading_notes.layout: Predominantly two-column main paper; References are single-column pages 11–13. No appendix/supplementary material is present in the verified 13-page PDF.
reading_notes.abstract_function_order: object_scope → problem_gap → mechanism diagnosis → core_idea → method → data/robustness → result/impact
reading_notes.theory_count: Five numbered displayed equations and one Lemma; no theorem, proposition, corollary, proof, or pseudocode algorithm.
reading_notes.statistics: No hypothesis test, bootstrap, Bayesian analysis, regression, confidence interval, or error bar is reported; aggregation is primarily mean/median/threshold point estimates.
reading_notes.lexical_notes: Frequent domain terms are normal, shading, sequence, geometry, light, material, diffusion, dataset, and estimation. Hyphenated terms such as image-to-video and state-of-the-art create tokenization risks.
